ابدأ الاعتذار بـ I am sorry. بعد because: Start an apology with I am sorry. Follow because with a clause containing a subject and verb: because the bus was late. Because of takes a noun phrase: because of the traffic. Keep the two patterns distinct.
ابدأ البريد بسبب واضح باستخدام I am writ: Open with a clear purpose using I am writing to followed by a verb, or regarding followed by a noun. Make your request specific and include a reply deadline when needed. Look forward to takes an -ing form such as hearing because to is a preposition here. Close with a suitable phrase such as Kind regards and your name.
ابدأ التقييم بما لاحظته فعلًا، ثم اذكر أ: Start a review with what you actually observed, then explain its effect and your overall view. Overall summarizes the experience; although connects contrasting ideas. A drawback is a specific disadvantage, while overpriced judges a price as too high for the value. ابدأ الرسالة بتحية، ثم I am writing abou: Begin with a greeting, use I am writing about to name the topic, and close with a phrase such as Kind regards. About introduces the topic. To request an answer, say reply to my email, not reply my email.
ابدأ السؤال عن عادة بـ Do ثم الفاعل ثم ا: Ask about a habit with Do, the subject and the base verb: Do you speak English? Short answers are Yes, I do and No, I don't. A question needs the auxiliary pattern, not just statement word order.
ابدأ السؤال عن فعل ماضٍ بـ Did ثم الفاعل: Ask about a past action with Did, the subject and the base verb. Short answers are Yes, I did and No, I didn't. Do not add Did to a be question such as Were you tired?; be uses a different pattern.
ابدأ الطلب المهذب بـ Can you ثم الفعل بص: Start a polite request with Can you followed by a base verb such as repeat or say. Do not add to after can. Repeat asks for the words again; louder asks for more volume. Choose the request that matches your need.

اسأل What color is it? عن اللون. dark bl: Ask What color is it? about colour. Dark blue and light blue describe different shades; dark or light comes before the colour. Dark can also mean without light in a room, so use context to identify the meaning.
اسأل Where is ثم اسم الشيء المفرد. أجب ب: Ask Where is followed by a singular object. Answer with its location, here for a place near you, or there for another place. Where asks about location; here can answer that question. Similar spelling does not make them the same word.

استخدم How many قبل اسم جمع للسؤال عن ال: Use How many before a plural noun to ask about a number: How many pens? Add are there to ask how many are present. In the answer, use There is for one and There are for more than one.

استخدم I am مع tired وsick لوصف حالتك، ل: Use I am with tired and sick to describe your condition, but I have with pain because it is a noun. To name the painful part, say My head hurts or My leg hurts; this singular subject takes the verb ending s.
استخدم I have عند الحديث عن إخوتك: I hav: Use I have to talk about siblings: I have one brother. Use a singular noun after one and a plural noun after two. Older and younger describe age; an older brother is not necessarily taller.
استخدم I want مع اسم المشروب للتعبير عن: Use I want with a drink to say what you want, and add please to be polite. Water, tea and milk are uncountable when referring to the drinks generally. To name a serving, say a cup of tea.
استخدم It is مع صفة الطقس: It is hot. لا: Use It is with a weather adjective: It is hot. Keep It even though Arabic expresses the subject differently. Warm usually describes a lower temperature than hot. Hot can also describe a drink.
استخدم There is مع قطعة أثاث واحدة وTher: Use There is for one item and There are for more than one, then give the location. Upstairs and downstairs can be adverbs without in before them. Downstairs means on a lower floor, not necessarily in a basement.
استخدم Would you like to مع فعل لدعوة شخ: Use Would you like to with a verb to invite someone to an activity: to join us. Use Would you like with a noun when offering something: some tea. Accept with Yes, I'd love to, or decline politely.
استخدم a blessing in disguise في موقف تد: Use a blessing in disguise in a practice scenario where a cancelled meeting allowed an error to be found before a presentation, without generalizing to every setback.
استخدم a أوan مع اسم المهنة المفرد: a nu: Use a or an with a singular job title: a nurse, an engineer. Name the workplace with works in a factory or works at a hotel. A shift is a scheduled period of work, not the person's occupation.
استخدم by bus أو by car لوصف وسيلة الموا: Use by bus or by car to name a means of transport, without a or the after by in this pattern. You can use walk with a destination: walk to work. The phrase for walking is on foot, not by foot.
استخدم have مع أسماء الأعراض: a headache: Use have with symptom nouns such as a headache or a cough, and feel with an adjective such as unwell. Sore throat describes discomfort without identifying its cause. Join symptoms with and when reporting how you feel.
استخدم have مع اسم العرض: a headache أوa: Use have with a symptom noun: a headache or a fever, and feel with an adjective: tired or sick. Do not say I am a headache; that identifies you as a headache rather than describing how you feel.
استخدم he عند الحديث عن رجل أو ولد، وshe: Use he for a man or boy and she for a woman or girl; both take is. Use we when you are part of the group and they for a group you are talking about; both take are.
استخدم is مع صفة مثل tall، وhas مع اسم م: Use is with an adjective such as tall and has with a noun such as hair or beard. Hair as a whole is uncountable: short black hair without a. Put length and then colour before hair to make the description specific.

استخدم on مع أسماء الأيام: on Tuesday، ل: Use on with day names: on Tuesday, but omit on before next Tuesday. English day names begin with a capital letter. Link the day to a plan with be going to followed by the activity.
استخدم play مع ألعاب مثل football، وgo م: Use play with games such as football, go with activities such as swimming, and do with exercise. A team is a group of players; a club can be the organisation running the activity. Join takes the group directly without to.

استخدم الماضي المستمر للخلفية التي كانت: Use the past continuous for an ongoing background and the past simple for a new event: I was waiting when she called. استخدم الماضي المستمر للخلفية: I was rid: Use the past continuous for the background: I was riding, and the past simple for the sudden event: I fell. Suddenly marks an unexpected event but does not explain its cause. Add a specific result or response after recounting it.
استخدم الماضي لسرد العطلة: visited وstay: Use past forms to recount a weekend: visited, stayed and enjoyed. After Did, the verb returns to enjoy. Catch up socially means exchange news after time apart, and get together means meet for company or a shared activity.

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Say pay by card and pay in cash. In this situation, change means the money returned after you pay, not the action of changing something. Money is uncountable in this everyday use.
الهدف: أن تسأل عن عدد الأشياء.\n\nالجملة:

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Use How many before a plural noun to ask about a number: How many pens? Add are there to ask how many are present. In the answer, use There is for one and There are for more than one.
الهدف: أن تسأل عن لون متاح.\n\nالجملة ال:
Objective: To ask about an available color.

Model sentence: Is this jacket available in black?

New words:
• available — متاح
• jacket — سترة
• black — أسود

• color — لون

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Available means the item can be obtained or used. Ask Is this jacket available in black? using in before the colour. Availability does not tell you whether the item is cheap or expensive.
الهدف: أن تسأل عن موعد القطار.\n\nالجملة:
Objective: To ask about the train time.

Model sentence: What time does the train leave?

New words:
• train — قطار
• leave — يغادر
• station — محطة
• platform — رصيف
• arrive — يصل
• late — متأخر

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Leave and arrive refer to different ends of a journey. After does, use leave without s. The simple present can describe a scheduled train time: The train leaves at ten.
الهدف: أن تسأل عن موقع شيء.\n\nالجملة ال:
Objective: To ask about the location of something.

Model sentence: Where is my bag? It is here.

New words:
• where — أين
• here — هنا
• there — هناك
• find — يجد
• look — ينظر
• inside — بالداخل

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Ask Where is followed by a singular object. Answer with its location, here for a place near you, or there for another place. Where asks about location; here can answer that question. Similar spelling does not make them the same word.
الهدف: أن تستخدم was وwere مع الضمائر.\n:
Objective: To use was and were with pronouns.

Model sentence: They were at home last night.

New words:
• were — صيغة الماضي من be مع you وwe وthey
• last night — الليلة الماضية
• home — المنزل
• they — هم
• yesterday — أمس
• together — معًا

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Use was with I, he, she and it, and were with you, we and they. You takes were even when addressing one person. Last night does not need at before it.
الهدف: أن تستخدم أساليب الإقناع المختلفة:
Objective: To use different persuasion techniques to influence your audience effectively.

Model sentence: A compelling example can attract attention, but the argument also needs reliable evidence.

New words:
• win someone over — يكسب تأييد أحدهم
• appeal to emotions — يخاطب العواطف
• compelling — مقنع للغاية
• credibility — المصداقية
• back up a claim — يدعم ادعاءً
• sway opinion — يؤثر في الرأي ويغيّره

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Effective persuasion connects the audience's interests with evidence relevant to the claim. Compelling means strongly convincing, but emotional impact does not establish truth. Back up a claim means support it with appropriate reasons or data, while credibility depends partly on accuracy and transparency. When using a personal story, identify it as an example rather than automatically generalizing it.
الهدف: أن تستخدم افتتاحًا وختامًا بسيطين:
Objective: To use a simple opening and closing.

Model sentence: Hello, I am writing about tomorrow’s meeting.

New words:
• writing — أكتب
• about — بشأن
• email — بريد إلكتروني
• send — يرسل
• regards — تحيات (في ختام الرسالة)
• reply — يرد

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Begin with a greeting, use I am writing about to name the topic, and close with a phrase such as Kind regards. About introduces the topic. To request an answer, say reply to my email, not reply my email.
Objective: To use red, blue, and green.

Model sentence: The bag is green.

New words:
• red — أحمر
• blue — أزرق
• green — أخضر
• yellow — أصفر
• brown — بنّي
• pink — وردي

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A colour can follow is: The bag is green, or come before a noun: a green bag. Green does not change for feminine or plural nouns as Arabic adjectives do. Follow the colour named in the sentence without needing a picture.
Objective: To use the simple present with I and we.

Model sentence: We study English every day.

New words:
• every day — كل يوم
• study — يدرس
• we — نحن
• I — أنا
• live — يعيش
• often — كثيرًا ما

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Use the base verb with I, we, you and they in the simple present: We study. Every day is two words meaning each day; everyday as one word is an adjective, as in everyday life.
Objective: To use an appropriate greeting when meeting someone.

Model sentence: Hello, I am Abdullah.

New words:
• hello — مرحبًا
• I — أنا
• am — فعل ربط مع I
• hi — أهلاً
• good morning — صباح الخير
• welcome — مرحبًا بك

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Use hello in many situations and hi in friendly conversation. To give your name, use I am followed by your name. English needs am here, although Arabic has no matching verb in the present-tense sentence.
الهدف: أن تستخدم ضميري هو وهي.\n\nالجملة:
Objective: To use the pronouns he and she.

Model sentence: She is a student.

New words:
• he — هو
• she — هي
• student — طالب / طالبة
• we — نحن
• they — هم / هن
• teacher — معلم

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Use he for a man or boy and she for a woman or girl; both take is. Use we when you are part of the group and they for a group you are talking about; both take are.
الهدف: أن تستخدم فعلًا ماضيًا شائعًا غير:
Objective: To use a common irregular past verb.

Model sentence: I went to the store after work.

New words:
• went — ذهب
• store — متجر
• after — بعد
• bought — اشترى
• market — سوق
• yesterday — أمس

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Went is the past form of go; do not say goed. Use to before a destination: went to the store. After work places the event after working, and yesterday can identify the day.
الهدف: أن تستخدم فعلًا ماضيًا منتظمًا.\n:
Objective: To use a regular past verb.

Model sentence: We watched a movie on Friday.

New words:
• watched — شاهد
• movie — فيلم
• Friday — الجمعة
• played — لعب
• last week — الأسبوع الماضي
• cooked — طبخ

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Add ed to regular verbs such as watch and play to form the past. Watched does not change with I, we or she. Use on before a day name, but use last week without on.
الهدف: أن تستخدم لغة محفّزة لرفع معنويات:
Objective: To use motivating language to boost your team's morale and enhance its performance.

Model sentence: Specific thanks can boost morale by showing that careful work is noticed.

New words:
• boost morale — يرفع المعنويات
• incentive — حافز
• recognize achievements — يقدّر الإنجازات
• engagement — الانخراط والتفاعل
• foster — يعزّز ويرعى
• rally — يحشد ويوحّد

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Distinguish an incentive, a specific motivator, from morale, the group's confidence or spirits, and engagement, involvement in work. When recognizing achievement, identify the action and its impact instead of giving generic praise. Recognize achievements without ignoring obstacles; ask what support is needed and connect encouragement to an understandable, realistic goal.
الهدف: أن تستنتج وتخمّن بناءً على الأدلة:
Objective: To infer and guess based on the available evidence using modal verbs of probability.

Model sentence: Judging by the empty parking lot, the office must have closed early today.

New words:
• must have — لا بدّ أنه قد
• judging by — بالنظر إلى
• presumably — على الأرجح
• infer — يستنتج
• it stands to reason — من المنطقي
• draw a conclusion — يستخلص نتيجة

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Must have plus a past participle expresses a strong inference about the past, not a past obligation; had to can express the latter. Judging by names the evidence, while presumably leaves room for error. Separate observation from inference and consider an alternative explanation before drawing a conclusion, especially with ambiguous clues such as silence.
الهدف: أن تسجّل الدخول إلى الفندق.\n\nال:
Objective: To check in at the hotel.

Model sentence: I have a reservation for two nights.

New words:
• reservation — حجز
• night — ليلة
• hotel — فندق
• room — غرفة
• key — مفتاح
• check in — يسجّل الوصول (إلى الفندق)

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A reservation is a booking, and check in means register your arrival at the hotel. Use for with the length of a stay: for two nights. Use plural nights after two and singular night after one.
الهدف: أن تسمي أثاثًا بسيطًا.\n\nالجملة:
Objective: To name simple furniture.

Model sentence: The chair is in the room.

New words:
• bed — سرير
• chair — كرسي
• table — طاولة
• sofa — أريكة
• lamp — مصباح
• shelf — رف

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A bed is for sleeping, a chair for sitting, and a sofa usually seats more than one person. Use the for a particular object: the chair. Say in the room for its location inside a room and on the table for something on the tabletop.
الهدف: أن تسمي أجزاء جسم أساسية.\n\nالجم:
Objective: To name basic body parts.

Model sentence: This is my hand.

New words:
• head — رأس
• hand — يد
• arm — ذراع
• leg — ساق
• foot — قدم
• finger — إصبع

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A hand and an arm are different body parts. Use my when naming your own body parts: my hand. The plurals are hands and arms, but the plural of foot is feet, not foots.
الهدف: أن تسمي أدوات الدراسة الأساسية.\n:
Objective: To name basic study supplies.

Model sentence: This is a pen.

New words:
• pen — قلم حبر
• paper — ورق
• desk — مكتب
• pencil — قلم رصاص
• notebook — دفتر
• ruler — مسطرة

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A pen uses ink; a pencil is different. A notebook is a book for writing. Use a with one countable object: a pen, a ruler. Paper as a material is uncountable; a piece of paper names one sheet.
الهدف: أن تسمي أشياء شخصية شائعة.\n\nالج:
Objective: To name common personal items.

Model sentence: My key is here.

New words:
• key — مفتاح
• phone — هاتف
• bag — حقيبة
• wallet — محفظة
• watch — ساعة يد
• glasses — نظارة

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A watch is worn on the wrist; a clock is a different kind of timepiece. Glasses meaning spectacles is grammatically plural in English: My glasses are here. Arabic may use a singular noun for the same object.
الهدف: أن تسمي أطعمة أساسية.\n\nالجملة ا:
Objective: To name basic foods.

Model sentence: I eat rice.

New words:
• bread — خبز
• rice — أرز
• eat — يأكل
• egg — بيضة
• meat — لحم
• soup — حساء

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Rice and bread are uncountable food nouns, so say I eat rice without a. Egg is countable: an egg for one and eggs for more than one. Use an because egg begins with a vowel sound.
الهدف: أن تسمي أعضاء الحواس الأساسية.\n\:
Objective: To name the basic sense organs.

Model sentence: I hear with my ears.

New words:
• eye — عين
• ear — أذن
• nose — أنف
• mouth — فم
• face — وجه
• hear — يسمع

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Eye and ear name different sense organs; their plurals are eyes and ears. Use with to name the body part used for an action: hear with my ears. Listen for the difference between singular eye and plural eyes.
الهدف: أن تسمي أماكن عامة مهمة.\n\nالجمل:
Objective: To name important public places.

Model sentence: The hospital is there.

New words:
• hospital — مستشفى
• park — حديقة
• there — هناك
• bank — بنك
• street — شارع
• here — هنا

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A hospital, a park and a bank have different purposes. Use here or there after is to identify a location briefly. To say what you do inside a park, use in the park: play in the park.
الهدف: أن تسمي الأشخاص بكلمات أساسية.\n\:
Objective: To name people with basic words.

Model sentence: The woman is here.

New words:
• man — رجل
• woman — امرأة
• person — شخص
• boy — ولد
• girl — بنت
• people — ناس

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Man and woman describe adults; boy and girl describe children. Person means one individual, and its usual plural is people. Say one person and two people rather than adding s in this everyday context.
الهدف: أن تسمي الإخوة والأخوات.\n\nالجمل:
Objective: To name brothers and sisters.

Model sentence: I have one brother.

New words:
• brother — أخ
• sister — أخت
• have — لديه
• baby — رضيع
• older — أكبر سنًا
• younger — أصغر سنًا

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Use I have to talk about siblings: I have one brother. Use a singular noun after one and a plural noun after two. Older and younger describe age; an older brother is not necessarily taller.
الهدف: أن تسمي المنزل والغرفة.\n\nالجملة:
Objective: To name the house and the room.

Model sentence: This is my room.

New words:
• house — منزل
• room — غرفة
• door — باب
• window — نافذة
• wall — حائط
• kitchen — مطبخ

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A house is a building, a room is part of it, and a kitchen is a type of room. Say in the house or in my room. Do not add the before my; my room already identifies the room.
الهدف: أن تسمي الوالدين.\n\nالجملة النمو:
Objective: To name the parents.

Model sentence: This is my mother.

New words:
• mother — أم
• father — أب
• family — عائلة
• parents — والدان
• son — ابن
• daughter — ابنة

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Mother means a female parent and father means a male parent. Parents refers to them together and is plural. Put my before the family word to identify your relationship: my mother. Use are with parents, not is.
الهدف: أن تسمي ثلاث فواكه شائعة.\n\nالجم:
Objective: To name three common fruits.

Model sentence: The apple is red.

New words:
• apple — تفاحة
• banana — موزة
• orange — برتقالة
• grape — عنبة
• lemon — ليمونة
• fruit — فاكهة

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
For one piece of fruit, say an apple or an orange, but a banana. Choose a or an by the first sound. Fruit is a general word for the food, while apple and banana are countable names of individual fruits.
الهدف: أن تسمي مكانين شائعين.\n\nالجملة:
Objective: To name two common places.

Model sentence: The school is near my house.

New words:
• school — مدرسة
• store — متجر
• place — مكان
• market — سوق
• house — منزل
• here — هنا

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A school, a store and a market are different places. To locate one place in relation to another, use near followed by the place: near my house. Do not add to after near in this simple pattern.
الهدف: أن تسمي ملابس أساسية.\n\nالجملة ا:
Objective: To name basic clothes.

Model sentence: My shirt is blue.

New words:
• shirt — قميص
• shoes — أحذية
• clothes — ملابس
• hat — قبعة
• dress — فستان
• wear — يرتدي

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Shirt is singular: My shirt is blue. Shoes and clothes are plural and take are. Use wear for clothing you have on as a habit; carry does not mean wearing a shirt.
الهدف: أن تسمي نشاطين دراسيين.\n\nالجملة:
Objective: To name two study activities.

Model sentence: I read a book.

New words:
• read — يقرأ
• write — يكتب
• study — يدرس
• book — كتاب
• pen — قلم
• learn — يتعلم

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Read and write name different activities. Study describes spending time on learning; learn describes gaining knowledge or a skill. Use with to name the tool you write with: write with a pen.
الهدف: أن تشارك في اتخاذ القرارات الجماع:
Objective: To take part in group decision-making and evaluate options with professional language.

Model sentence: After weighing up the pros and cons, the board reached a consensus on the new strategy.

New words:
• weigh up the options — يوازن بين الخيارات
• reach a consensus — يتوصل إلى توافق
• pros and cons — الإيجابيات والسلبيات
• make a call — يتخذ قرارًا
• trade-off — مفاضلة بين مكسب وتضحية
• rule out — يستبعد

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A trade-off accepts a loss in one aspect for a gain in another, rather than simply comparing two options. Reach a consensus means find broad agreement without necessarily removing every reservation; rule out means exclude a possibility. Make a call can mean decide here, not telephone. State decision criteria and remaining uncertainty before announcing the outcome.
الهدف: أن تشرح المفاهيم العلمية وتقيّم ا:
Objective: To explain scientific concepts and evaluate evidence using the language of scientific inquiry.

Model sentence: A well-designed experiment can test a hypothesis, but its results still need careful interpretation.

New words:
• hypothesis — فرضية
• conduct research — يجري بحثًا
• evidence-based — قائم على الأدلة
• breakthrough — إنجاز علمي فارق
• peer review — مراجعة الأقران
• deduce — يستنتج

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
A hypothesis is a testable explanation or prediction, not a pre-established fact. Conduct research means investigate; peer review means specialist evaluation within a publication or assessment process, not a guarantee of infallibility. Evidence-based means grounded in examinable evidence. State whether results support a hypothesis and what limits them rather than claiming universal proof from one experiment.
الهدف: أن تشرح مشكلة طلب باختصار.\n\nالج:
Objective: To briefly explain a problem with an order.

Model sentence: I received the wrong item.

New words:
• received — استلم
• wrong — غير الصحيح / غير المطلوب
• customer service — خدمة العملاء
• refund — استرداد المال
• broken — مكسور
• complaint — شكوى

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
First state the problem factually: I received the wrong item. Then explain what you want. A wrong item is different from the one ordered; a broken item is damaged. These describe different problems.
الهدف: أن تشير إلى شيء قريب أو بعيد.\n\n:
Objective: To point to something near or far.

Model sentence: This is my book.

New words:
• this — هذا / هذه
• that — ذلك / تلك
• is — فعل ربط مع المفرد
• these — هذه / هؤلاء
• those — تلك / أولئك
• it — ضمير لغير العاقل

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Use this for one nearby thing and that for one distant thing; both take is. Use these for nearby plural things and those for distant plural things; both take are. The distinction is number and distance, not grammatical gender.
الهدف: أن تشير إلى يوم مضى.\n\nالجملة ال:
Objective: To refer to a past day.

Model sentence: I was busy yesterday.

New words:
• yesterday — أمس
• was — كان
• busy — مشغول
• tired — متعب
• happy — سعيد
• morning — صباح

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Yesterday refers to a finished day. To describe your condition yesterday, use was instead of am: I was busy. Do not put in or on before yesterday. It can come at the beginning or end of the sentence.
الهدف: أن تصف أساليب القيادة المختلفة وت:
Objective: To describe different leadership styles and discuss their advantages and disadvantages.

Model sentence: A successful leader knows when to take charge and when to step back and let the team decide.

New words:
• take charge — يتولّى زمام الأمور
• lead by example — يقود بالقدوة
• hands-on — مشارك مباشرة في العمل
• decisive — حاسم
• visionary — صاحب رؤية
• step back — يتراجع ويفسح المجال

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Hands-on describes direct involvement in details, not automatically excessive interference. Take charge means assume leadership; step back means allow others space. Decisive suggests reaching decisions firmly with enough information, not necessarily refusing consultation. When comparing styles, connect their benefits to the context and team's experience rather than presenting either as universally best.
الهدف: أن تصف أعراضًا بسيطة بجمل واضحة.\:
Objective: Describe simple symptoms in clear sentences.

Model sentence: I have a headache.

New words:
• headache — صداع
• feel unwell — يشعر بتوعك
• symptom — عرض مرضي
• fever — حُمّى
• cough — سُعال
• sore throat — ألم في الحلق
• medicine — دواء

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Use have with symptom nouns such as a headache or a cough, and feel with an adjective such as unwell. Sore throat describes discomfort without identifying its cause. Join symptoms with and when reporting how you feel.
الهدف: أن تصف الاتجاهات الصاعدة والهابطة:
Objective: To describe upward, downward, and stable trends with precise, professional language.

Model sentence: The figures show an upward trend in the first quarter, followed by a stable period.

New words:
• rise steadily — يرتفع بثبات
• level off — يستقرّ ويثبت
• plummet — يهبط بشدة
• fluctuate — يتذبذب
• upward trend — اتجاه تصاعدي
• peak — يبلغ ذروته

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Separate direction, pace, and period: rise steadily means increase regularly, plummet means drop sharply, and fluctuate means move up and down. Level off means stabilize after change, not continue rising slowly. Peak means reach the highest point within the displayed period. Use figures and a time range to justify the description; a trend alone does not identify its cause.
الهدف: أن تصف الطقس البارد أو الممطر.\n\:
Objective: To describe cold or rainy weather.

Model sentence: It is cold and rainy.

New words:
• cold — بارد
• rain — مطر
• cloud — سحابة
• wind — رياح
• snow — ثلج
• winter — شتاء

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Rain is a noun; rainy is an adjective. Describe the weather with It is rainy, not It is rain. Join two adjectives with and to describe both cold weather and rain.

Objective: To describe a common health symptom.

Model sentence: I have a headache and feel tired.

• headache — صداع

الهدف: أن تصف علاقاتك بالآخرين وتعبّر عن:

Objective: To describe the act of opening and closing something.

Model sentence: I open the door.

Objective: To describe what you do in the evening.

• breakfast — الفطور

• early — مبكرًا
• alarm clock — منبّه
• morning — صباح

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Usually normally comes before the main verb: I usually wake up. Use at before a clock time such as seven and in before a period such as the morning. The sentence describes a regular habit, not just an action happening now.
الهدف: أن تضيف s للفعل مع he وshe.\n\nال:
Objective: To add s to the verb with he and she.

Model sentence: He works in a bank.

New words:
• works — يعمل
• bank — بنك
• in — في
• she — هي
• teacher — معلّم
• office — مكتب

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

• artificial intelligence — الذكاء الاصطناعي

Notice how the language works:
Automation means performing tasks automatically; not all automation is artificial intelligence. Job displacement concerns roles lost or work shifted as methods change. • rote memorization — الحفظ الآلي بالتكرار

• overhaul the system — يعيد هيكلة النظام
• equitable access — الوصول العادل

Notice how the language works:
Curriculum concerns learning content and organization; assessment concerns judging performance. They are related but not interchangeable. A reform proposal should name a problem, action, and method for assessing effects and costs rather than make an unlimited promise.

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
For an unreal past, use if plus had and a past participle, followed by would have and a past participle for the imagined result. الهدف: أن يتمكن المتعلم من وصف تجاربه ال:

Structure a leadership interview answer around the situation, your responsibility, your action and a verifiable result. Spearhead means lead an initiative; oversee means supervise its execution. Concision removes repetition without removing a condition that changes the meaning. الهدف: أن يحكي المتعلم موقفًا غير متوقع:

Use the past continuous for an ongoing background and the past simple for a new event: I was waiting when she called. Bump into can mean meet someone unexpectedly, not literally collide. الهدف: أن يحل المتعلم مشكلة بسيطة مع جار:

When raising a problem with a neighbour, describe the behaviour, time, and effect rather than judging the person. Complain about names the issue; complain to names the person receiving the complaint. الهدف: أن يحلل المتعلم أثر المؤثرين والخ:
Objective: To analyse how influencers and algorithms shape people's opinions.

Model sentence: An algorithm may reinforce familiar views by repeatedly recommending similar content.

• algorithm — خوارزمية

Notice how the language works:
Go viral describes rapid or widespread sharing, not truth. Clickbait attracts clicks by withholding information or exaggerating. An echo chamber reinforces similar views, while a filter bubble narrows exposure through personalization; they can overlap. Analyse the headline, source, and context instead of treating share counts as proof.
الهدف: أن يحلل المتعلم كيف تغيّر الابتكا:

Listen to the model, then practise the words in the exercises.

Notice how the language works:
Disrupt means disturb or substantially change an established pattern, not every minor update. An incumbent is an established participant, while a legacy system is inherited infrastructure still in use and possibly essential. Obsolete means no longer suitable for the relevant need, not merely old. Test a paradigm-shift claim against changes in practice rather than marketing language about novelty.
الهدف: أن يحلل المتعلم كيف تغيّر صياغة ا:

Notice how the language works:
Framing selects an angle; omission can distort understanding even when individual sentences remain true. A baseline supplies the comparison needed for change.
